questions.q: What is the real relationship between `kb_knowledge_base` and `kb_knowledge`?
options: `kb_knowledge_base` is the container (one Knowledge Base); `kb_knowledge` is each individual article, referencing exactly one Knowledge Base
They are the same table under two different names
`kb_knowledge` is the container, and `kb_knowledge_base` is each individual article
`kb_knowledge_base` only exists for reporting and holds no real records
questions.explain: The Knowledge Base is the container record; every article record points back to exactly one of them.

questions.q: Why might a company implement a separate Self-Service Knowledge Base and IT Staff Knowledge Base?
options: To segment audiences at the container level — end users browsing one book, internal staff browsing a different one with more sensitive content
Because a single Knowledge Base cannot technically hold more than one article
Category fields cannot be reused across more than one Knowledge Base
Workflow state only functions correctly when there is exactly one Knowledge Base
questions.explain: Splitting Knowledge Bases by audience controls who can even browse a book, before any individual article's own permissions apply.

questions.q: Which of these is a real field on a `kb_knowledge` article record?
options: Workflow state
Zoom meeting ID
Incident priority
CAB approval date
questions.explain: Workflow state (Draft, Review, Published, Retired) is a real field tracking the article's lifecycle.

questions.q: What does the Category field do on a `kb_knowledge` record?
options: It groups related articles together inside one Knowledge Base, like folders inside a book
It determines which Knowledge Base the article belongs to
It sets the article's Workflow state automatically
It replaces the need for a Knowledge Base reference entirely
questions.explain: Category is a taxonomy field for organizing articles within a single Knowledge Base; the Knowledge Base reference field is what assigns the article to its book.

questions.q: How do Knowledge Base-level permissions and article-level overrides work together?
options: The Knowledge Base sets a default Can Read / Can Contribute baseline for every article inside it; an individual article can override that default when it genuinely needs a narrower audience
Article-level overrides always replace the Knowledge Base's permissions for every article in that Knowledge Base
Knowledge Base-level permissions only apply to Draft articles
There is no real permission mechanism at the Knowledge Base level, only at the article level
questions.explain: Setting the default once at the Knowledge Base, and reserving overrides for the exception, keeps permissions manageable as article count grows.
